about: Stages and timing for the search-vs-category playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: match
stages.do: Compare the busiest category-name searches with their category pages, add the redirect and align-ranking findings, and ask the user which redirect to make.

stages.name: fix
stages.do: Plan an exact-match redirect from the chosen query to its category page, create it switched off, and switch it on, each batch after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the match stage found no category search to redirect.

stages.name: measure
stages.do: Check the redirect helped: the category page's visits and conversion against the site-wide trend, with the redirect and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: no redirect went live, so there is nothing to measure.
the fix stage was skipped, so no redirect went live.

notes.measure_after_days: Days after the fix stage finishes (the redirect was switched on) before the measure stage is due. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes).
